prompt: Simplify $\dfrac{(2x^{3}y^{-2})^{3}}{4x^{-1}y^{2}}$, giving your answer with positive exponents.
markscheme:
$(2x^{3}y^{-2})^{3}=8x^{9}y^{-6}$ **(A1)**

$\dfrac{8x^{9}y^{-6}}{4x^{-1}y^{2}}=2x^{9-(-1)}y^{-6-2}=2x^{10}y^{-8}$ **(M1)**

$=\dfrac{2x^{10}}{y^{8}}$ **(A1)**

**Common mistake:** cubing only the variables and leaving the 2 as 2 — the power applies to every factor in the bracket.

prompt:
**(a)** Write down the value of $\log_{10}0.001$. **[1]**

**(b)** Write down the value of $\ln\left(e^{5}\right)$. **[1]**

**(c)** Solve $e^{2x}=7$, giving your answer in exact form. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $0.001=10^{-3}$, so $\log_{10}0.001=-3$ **(A1)**

**(b)** $\ln$ and $e^{x}$ are inverse functions: $\ln(e^{5})=5$ **(A1)**

**(c)** $2x=\ln7$, so $x=\dfrac{\ln7}{2}$ **(A1)**

A logarithm answers the question “what power?”: $\log_{10}y=x$ means exactly $10^{x}=y$.
